beta_new: Climb the trough past a bolt to a ledge, then go up cracks and a dihedral to a small overhang. Pass the overhang on the left and climb the chimney to a ledge with a tree. The third pitch walks right into a gully to the foot of the friction slab, and the last climbs the face, clipping two bolts, to the top.

moves.from: The summit of the Head is a scramble from there.

beta_new: Climb the east-facing side of the boulder, clipping two bolts, to the top.

moves.from: Descend with the same single-rope rappel used for Energizer.

beta_new: This is an optional extra pitch above the third-pitch belay of The Classic. A party that has had enough, or is worried about weather, can scramble off to the rappel station instead; otherwise it gives you one more fine pitch.
Start in the middle of the northeast face and climb straight up past the bolt to the top. For the variation, step off the boulder on the north side onto the northwest face and join the regular route.
Begin at the right end of the lower crag and climb the flared crack into the boulder enclave. Move left across onto the face and go past a bolt to the top.
Step off the large boulder lying right of the big roof and climb the gentle face, trending slightly left, to the arete. Stay on the face just right of the arete up to the rappel anchor.

Climb the slab to a second bolt at an overhang and turn it for the crux. Go on to the bolt where the traverse of E.S.A.D. passes, then take the middle of the face separating those two routes to the top.
Follow the leftmost bolted line on the long cliff band, beside the gully. The moves ease off the further left you stay.
Reach the anchor by crossing the slabs south from close to the summit of Fly By, rappel in, then climb back up the face and the resonant flake or crack, passing two horizontal cracks and two bolts.
Begin a bit right of the middle and angle leftward and upward to the center of the face, clipping two bolts and using the xenoliths as holds. Test each hold before trusting it.

Start in the short crack that arcs rightward and follow it, then ease back left along an indistinct thin crack to a big flake with a crack. Finish the pitch up lichen-covered rock past a horn to a belay bolt.

Climb the face to a bolt, trend upward and rightward to some little ledges that slope down and a second bolt, then move left and follow the obvious water-worn groove up to a crack. Follow that crack up into the large stand of trees at the top.
Climb the short face past the bolt, which is where the crux comes, to a small ledge. Then take the wide vertical crack above it to the top.
Start at the base of the smooth slab, climb the small dihedral, then carry on up the face, clipping two bolts, to the top.
Climb the seam up and leftward, then the face, clipping two bolts, to a horizontal crack. Get onto the big boulder balanced on a ledge and finish up the face, clipping two further bolts.
Climb the bolted face beside the block that sits under Sweet Surprise, on its right. The sequence above the second bolt is where the difficulty lies.
Begin on top of the V-shaped lip and climb the face to a bolt, then continue to the left end of a horizontal crack. Move past the crack and finish up the face to the left of the two bolts.
Go up the steep face lying between Slot and Limbo, clipping three bolts on the way.

Begin within a steep corner, and once at its top go rightward and up the bolted face. Later slide leftward round the arete into a corner until you can get back onto the arete, then slant rightward to a crack to sidestep the poorly protected arete.

Start from the boulder at the very bottom of the north face, climb to the highest horizontal crack and follow it left to the base of a crack that arches rightward. Follow it to an alcove with a bolt, then leave leftward and upward to the bulge where a rappel bolt sits.
Go up the corner that faces left, clipping two bolts, to a roof, traverse beneath it to the third bolt, then take the thin crack to the top.
Start on the slab facing northeast, directly under Mickey Mantle and climb straight up the face, clipping two bolts, to the top.
Start beneath the smooth face to the right of Rurpture and climb past a bolt to join the crack shortly before the corner. Carry on over the little overhang, clipping a bolt, to the top.
Follow the crack system running up the middle of the face. Protection is scarce low down and becomes better as you gain height.
Work up beyond horizontal cracks to a bolted prow, then finish on the face above, clipping two more bolts on the way to the top.
Go up the trough, passing cracks, to a ledge and a bolt, then face climb through the second bolt to an undercling and the third bolt. Continue straight up the face above to the top.
Start where Rest In Peace starts, traverse in from the left, and climb the face, clipping one bolt, into the right-hand crack. Follow that crack to the top.
Climb a short corner to an overhanging flake that you layback, then keep going beyond a single bolt before following crack and face above.
On the west face's right edge, one bolt and one pin lead up into a crack system. Where the crack runs out you can either pull over the bulge or escape leftward to Rabbit Tracks.
Begin ten feet to the right of Banana Crack and climb the face past a bolt to a horizontal crack, and finish exactly as Banana Crack does.

Start at the right side of the southeast face, go up the slender crack and the face to the corner, then follow the corner to the top. Double ropes are the safeguard against rope damage should a fall swing you round the corner.

moves.from: Double ropes are the safeguard against rope damage should a fall swing you round the corner.

value.text: Double ropes, to guard against rope damage if a fall swings you round the corner.

beta_new: On the first pitch climb the loose gully with its minor overhangs, until a rightward traverse leads to a small belay ledge. The second pitch crosses rightward onto the exposed face and go straight up the water chute to a bolt in the gully, then scramble up the gully to the summit.
Start up Swept Away, reaching the stance above the arch, then continue on Ways itself. Tiny wired nuts are useful on the face over the arch.

Share the opening with South Gully and follow it until you can traverse left along a horizontal crack to a small ledge under a bolt. Above that, a face with four bolts leads up to the top of the West Summit.
Start twenty feet right of Changes in Latitude beneath a small undercling. Climb the face, clipping three bolts, to a horizontal crack, then carry on up the face above it to the top.

Start on top of the big standing flake in the gully and climb the crack system above to a horizontal crack. Traverse left along it until below a bolt, then work up the face, well right of the pair of bolts.
Follow the line of bolts right of Perspective until it crosses Perspective at an angling crack. A finger-size nut or cam protects the moves through the horizontal crack.
Begin on the east side and climb the face, clipping two bolts, straight to the top.

Begin at the right side of the south face and angle leftward up the face, clipping two bolts, to the roof's left end. A single distinctive move takes you over it, and the belay with two bolts is just beyond.
Share the start with Birthday Party and follow the ramp rightward until you can climb the face above, clipping two bolts, to a roof. There, cross to the right and meet Dried Oatmeal for the finish.

Start at the highest point of the upper talus and climb the easy wide dihedral, trending left, to the base of the chimney. Follow the chimney, passing a bolt, to a broad ledge, then scramble up the gullies to the south and west to the summit.
